title: Nine Percent Battery
description: A 4 AM love song to a dying smoke detector. Rubella can’t reach it; the chirp lands every 47 seconds and is the only in-tune pitch on the record.
stylePrompt:
Sincere indie-folk breakup ballad, 68 BPM, addressed to a smoke detector.
Nylon-string guitar close-mic'd with finger squeak left in, upright bass, one
brushed floor tom, no cymbals. Rubella singing at 4 AM volume — the volume you
use when the neighbors are asleep and you are not. Genuinely tender. No wink,
no comedy voice, no "funny song" phrasing; the joke is that the arrangement
never learns it is a joke. **Structural flaw:** the detector's low-battery
chirp lands every 47 seconds — it does not fall on a bar line, a beat, or a
lyric, and it never will. It is also the only perfectly in-tune pitch in the
recording (Bb6); tune the entire band six cents flat against it. Do not gate
it, do not quantize it, do not fade it under the vocal. Second voice optional:
the chirp is the duet partner. Ends on a chirp with no music under it. Runtime
~2:10–2:30.
lyrics:
[Intro — nylon guitar, one chirp before the downbeat]
(chirp)
Okay.
Okay, I heard you.

[Verse 1]
Nine percent battery, ceiling of the hall
Fourteen feet of nothing between me and the wall
I have a chair. The chair has opinions.
The ladder is downstairs and the stairs are downstairs too
You have been honest with me every forty-seven seconds
Which is more than anyone I know has ever done

[Pre-Chorus]
I'm not asking you to stop
I'm asking what you want
And I already know
And I can't reach it

[Chorus]
Nine percent battery
You are the only thing in this building telling me the truth
No committee, no laminate, no memo, no excuse
Just a small square saying: soon, soon, soon
I would save you if the ceiling were lower
I would save you if I were taller
(chirp)
I know.

[Verse 2]
I bought the nine-volt in November
It's in a drawer with the keys to a door I don't have
Every night I plan the rescue
Every morning I forget the drawer exists
You never bring it up
You just keep the appointment

[Bridge — half-time, floor tom only]
Everyone in Unit 4B says the sound is haunted
Everyone in Unit 6 says it's the pipes
Madelyn issued a notice about "recurring tones"
Nobody said it was dying
Nobody said it was doing its job

[Final Chorus]
Nine percent battery
Nine percent is still percent
Nine percent is more than the elevator has
More than the boiler, more than me
You will outlast the smoke you were built for
You will outlast the hallway light
You will outlast this song by about four chirps
(chirp)

[Outro — guitar stops, chirp continues alone]
(chirp)
(chirp)
Goodnight.
(chirp)
notes:
## What the song is
A love song to a dying smoke detector, played completely straight. Rubella
cannot reach it, will not replace it, and has stopped pretending either of
those is the point. The building is full of people announcing things that
aren't true; the one honest device in it is announcing its own death on a
fixed schedule. Nobody in the song laughs.
